subject: P0: Greenline - throughput/latency surge in us-west-2 and geo drain plan
messages:
From: Samir Rao <ops@greenline.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 08:12:34 -0000
Subject: P0: sudden 500/latency spike in us-west-2

Vivek / team,

We started seeing a broad increase in tail latency and 5xx rates for Redwood API traffic from our US-WEST-2 region ~08:00 UTC. Impact: our shipment tracking API (sync calls) is timing out; retries are queuing and throughput has dropped ~40%.

Attached is a quick Grafana screenshot and a heap dump from our side of the client (we instrumented more verbose retries at 07:58). Can you confirm whether there are any regional service disruptions, throttling, or routing changes from Redwood's side? We need an ETA — this is impacting live customers.

Samir Rao
Sr. Ops Engineer, Greenline Logistics
[sent from mobile]

Attachments: grafana_usw2_20280425_0805.png (image/png), throughput-heapdump-0808.txt (text/plain)

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I'm opening this as a P0 and looping in eng oncall. We're investigating for a regional capacity/queueing issue.

Immediate plan:
- Rishi: can you confirm whether we're seeing increased queue depth / token processing time on us-west2 inference pools?
- Laura: please surface any current routing/eviction actions or scheduled maintenance in the last 24h.
- Samir: we'll follow up with live updates — I'm setting a 15-min cadence. If you have a Slack channel we can drop into, please share.

I'll escalate to CS and Exec if this is impacting SLA.

— Vivek

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Samir Rao <ops@greenline.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 09:05:42 -0000
Subject: Re: P0: sudden 500/latency spike in us-west-2

Vivek / all,

Initial findings from the runtime metrics: there is a sharp increase in tail token latency starting 07:58 UTC for model-rw-13b variants in the us-west-2 dedicated pool. 5xxs appear correlated with renewing KV cache hot-shard reads and autoscale oscillation (rapid add/remove of workers) — likely a capacity pressure pattern, not a single-node crash.

Notes:
- CPU/GPU utilization on the pool is ~92% with sustained queue depth spikes.
- Inference kernel telemetry shows increased memcpy stalls when sequence lengths exceed expected distribution (Greenline's batch size spiked after a client-side config change at ~07:56).
- No automated maintenance windows reported for the pool.

Immediate recommendation: enable an emergency geo-drain from us-west-2 to us-west-1 (read-only routing to avoid stateful eviction), reduce max batch size for Greenline's route, and enable model-variant fallback to the 8-bit quantized replica to relieve memory pressure.

I'll prepare the drain play (steps + rollback) — Laura, can you prepare the route policy change and confirm rollback knobs?

Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

On Tue, Apr 25, 2028 at 08:25, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samir — thanks for the heads up...

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <ops@greenline.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 11:20:30 -0000
Subject: Re: P0: sudden 500/latency spike in us-west-2

Rishi / Vivek — agreed. I've drafted a minimal geo-drain play and validated the route change CLI against a staging account. Key points:

Planned action (starting 11:30 UTC):
1) Add a per-route policy for greenline-prod to prefer us-west-1 endpoints.
2) Apply prefix KV-cache warmup for us-west-1 to avoid cold-miss amplification.
3) Drop max_batch_size to 4 for Greenline's route until throughput stabilizes.
4) Enable variant-fallback: if quantized-8b is available, route there.
5) Monitor 5xx rate, tail latency, and queue depth at 1-min cadence.

Rollback: revert route policy and batch-size change. Full rollforward if 5xx < 0.5% and p99 latency drops below 400ms for 5 consecutive mins.

I'll execute the CLI steps at 11:30 and report back. Marissa, can you start the customer comms (short bulletin + executive note)?

Laura
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 12:40:05 -0000
Subject: Re: P0: sudden 500/latency spike in us-west-2

Samir — quick update and actions taken: we initiated the geo-drain at 11:31 UTC (us-west-2 -> us-west-1) and applied temporary route limits for Greenline-prod. Early telemetry: 5xx rate has dropped from ~3.8% to 0.7% and p99 latency improved ~45% in the first 8 mins. We're continuing to monitor and have enabled the quantized-8b fallback for further relief.

Attachments: geo-drain-playbook-v1.pdf (PDF) — contains CLI commands executed and rollback instructions.

Next steps:
- Marissa: sending an exec summary + customer bulletin to contracts@greenline.com (cc'ed).
- Rishi / Laura: please keep 15-min updates for next 2 hours and note any anomalies in SUP-4521.

Samir — apologies for the impact. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary and recommended long-term mitigations (route rate-limiter, model pinning, and quota smoothing). If you'd like a short bridge with execs, we can set one up this afternoon.

— Vivek
VP, Sales (escalation owner)
Redwood Inference
